findings.finding: Expectations have been reset: spot $96.6 is 38.5% below the 2026-10-13 high ($157.57), -26.2% over 20 days and back at the post-Q2 low ($97.63), ~36% under the $143-152 mean target, so the September analyst-day rally (+11-18%) is fully given back and the bar the market holds is lower than at the last three prints.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last three prints came off higher bases (Aug print after a run from the June low) and were all sold -8.9/-14.8/-10.3 (baseline); no print in the 3-event clean history was taken from a 38% drawdown.
findings.why_not_priced: The drawdown is priced by definition; what is not priced is how a beat-and-raise reads from here. If the market still held the September bar, the stock would not be sitting at the post-Q2 low with call IV above put IV (skew -8.04).
findings.independence: Baseline tape (run-up fields) and stockanalysis.com targets (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/P); most of the drawdown is shared with the AI-hardware selloff (Nvidia -32%, Dell ~-41%), so it is partly sector and not company-specific.

findings.finding: This name sells its beats: Q2 FY27 beat revenue by 7.5% ($1,185.9m vs $1,102.8m) and raised FY27 revenue by ~$590m yet fell 10.35% on negative FCF (-$238m vs +$227m expected) and margin; the two prints before fell 14.8% and 8.9%; 0 of 3 clean prints up.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats with guide raises: -10.3% (Aug 2026), -14.8% (May 2026), -8.9% (Feb 2026 per baseline ordering). The quality-of-beat lines (cash flow, gross margin, price-vs-units mix) drove the selling.
findings.why_not_priced: The pattern is public, but the option market currently pays for upside (skew -8.04) and the stock is at a low, which would look different if the market expected a fourth sold beat; the pattern says a revenue beat alone will not lift it.
findings.independence: Baseline history moves (-8.87, -14.81, -10.30); Motley Fool on the August week (https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/30/why-everpure-stock-plummeted-this-week/).

findings.finding: Revenue beat is the base case: in Q2 P beat consensus by 7.5% and the top of its own guide, about a third of growth has come from price increases (CEO on the Q1 call), and NAND/enterprise SSD contract prices kept rising through the fiscal quarter (Aug-Oct) and into Q4 (TrendForce: NAND +15-20% QoQ in 4Q26, enterprise SSD +15-28%), so Q3 revenue likely lands above the $1.33bn guide midpoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats of 7.5% (Q2) were sold -10%; a beat alone has not paid on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: The beat itself is expected (whisper $0.81 > $0.77); what is unpriced is only its size. Two-thirds of releases beat, and this name's are sold, so this is sized near zero.
findings.independence: Q2 beat vs consensus (TIKR, above); Sandisk Q1 FY27 datacenter revenue ~$4.8bn, growth ~40% pricing (https://fourweekmba.com/ai-sandisk-sales-hit-11b-at-an-85-margin-data-centers-44/). Shares the TrendForce/Sandisk pricing fact with the next finding, which carries the margin side.

findings.finding: Component cost inflation still running: TrendForce has 4Q26 enterprise SSD contracts +15-20% (Oct 30 update, down from a +23-28% Sept forecast) and Sandisk guided 84.5-85.5% gross margin for its next quarter; P chose to run product GM at the low end of 65-70% (66.2% in Q2), so rising NAND cost both lifts P's price-driven revenue and threatens a product GM print below 65%; net small positive because the price pass-through has so far been ahead of cost.
findings.link: P buys raw NAND for its DirectFlash modules; NAND makers (Sandisk, Kioxia, Micron, Samsung) are its input suppliers; P's March 2026 customer letter cited 300-900% input-cost inflation since mid-2025 and a ~40% list price increase.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 product GM 66.2% was cited as one cause of the -10% August reaction (Motley Fool); the April 2026 cost-squeeze letter day was -3.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: Analysts model GM at the guided low end; the deceleration of the enterprise SSD increase (23-28% forecast to 15-20%) is in an industry report, not in P previews, which still frame margin as a risk.
findings.independence: Proxy: industry series and a supplier's guide, not P's own number. Rallies.ai on the April letter (https://rallies.ai/news/everpure-stock-slides-as-management-flags-prolonged-ai-driven-component-cost-squeeze). Shares a document with the previous finding.

findings.finding: Cash-flow test: Q2 OCF -$136m and FCF -$238m (vs +$227m expected) from NAND pre-buys; the FY27 FCF guide of $600-800m needs roughly +$725-925m in H2 after H1 FCF of -$126m; with NAND prices still rising into Q4, continued pre-buying is plausible, so Q3 FCF short of a clear snapback or a cut to the FCF guide is the main downside risk; CFO said OCF should 'normalize over the next 2 quarters'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The FCF miss was the main driver of the -10.35% August reaction (TIKR).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced (stock at post-Q2 low); the FY FCF guide was reaffirmed and street FCF models still assume it, so a cut is not in the numbers. If it were priced, the skew would lean to puts rather than calls.
findings.independence: TIKR Q2 article (FCF vs expected, CFO quote); finviz/EW preview naming FCF as the test (https://finviz.com/news/420784/everpure-must-prove-its-guidance-leap-is-real-as-cash-flow-snap-back-faces-test). The continuation of pre-buys is my inference from NAND pricing, not a company statement.

findings.finding: Mid-quarter statement 2026-09-23 (analyst day, ~7 weeks into the Aug-Oct quarter): management reaffirmed FY27 revenue $5.03-5.07bn and issued a preliminary FY28 of $7.0-7.3bn revenue and $1.7-1.9bn op income vs street $6.14-6.5bn; stock rose 11-18% the next day.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The FY28 guide day itself was +11% to +18% (24/7 Wall St, TIKR); the gain has since been fully reversed.
findings.why_not_priced: A reaffirmation made with most of the quarter visible lowers the risk of a Q3 miss; the price has since round-tripped as if the FY28 target were doubted, so a reiteration of $7.0-7.3bn would be new comfort at this level.

findings.finding: Mid-quarter statement 2026-10-13 (investor update): Fusion customers at 2,300, adoption nearly doubled in six months; no guidance change.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Product/adoption metrics have not moved this stock on prints; the stock fell 9.86% the next day (2026-10-14) on a macro inflation selloff.
findings.why_not_priced: Small software adoption metric; not in previews. Barely bears on the reaction.

findings.finding: Next guide likely a revenue raise: guide raised at Q1 and Q2, reaffirmed 2026-09-23; Q3 beat flows through; Benzinga street Q4 $1.48bn sits about at the guide-implied Q4, while Earnings Whispers carries FY27 consensus at $5.29bn, above the $5.03-5.07bn guide, so the buy-side bar is a raise of ~$200m+.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide raises of ~$590m (Aug) and in May were both sold (-10.3%, -14.8%); a raise alone has not paid.
findings.why_not_priced: The street FY27 figure is disputed between sources ($5.29bn vs ~guide), so where the raise needs to land is not agreed; a raise above $5.2bn plus an FY28 reiteration would beat the lower of the two bars at a price that no longer holds the FY28 story.
findings.independence: Benzinga Q3/Q4 consensus (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/P/earnings-forecasts); Zacks: FY27 EPS estimates +13.4% over 90 days to $2.79 (https://zacks.com/stock/news/3022794/is-everpure-worth-buying-ahead-of-q3-earnings-as-valuation-stays-rich).

baseline_tension: The findings mostly agree with the upside-paid skew and cut against the -26% run-up (a reset that lowers the bar), but the name's own reaction history (three sold beat-and-raises) and the unproven FCF snapback cut the other way, so p_up stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (verified fact is not a reaction; this name sells beats): consensus-beat finding cut from +0.8 to +0.3; p_up moved from 52 to 51.

Rule 5 (proxy smaller): NAND-pricing counterparty finding +0.5 -> +0.3, Kioxia +0.2 -> +0.1, Meta +0.5 -> +0.3; FCF-guide-cut inference -1.5 -> -1.2 because the continued pre-buy is my inference, not a company statement.
Rule 6 (bar): revenue bar sourced to the company guide and two agreeing estimates, so sizes not capped; the EPS bar is disputed and no finding rests on it.

Rule 7 (positioning): short interest checked before the negatives; not crowded, so the negatives were left at size; the reaction-history negative is kept against the moderate upside skew because it is this name's own pattern.
Rules 3 and 9 left standing: no finding contradicts another after merging the margin and revenue sides of the NAND fact into separate lines with one shared document noted.
